story.title: Initialize Supabase Project & Client Integration
story.i_want: to set up a new Supabase project and integrate the Supabase client into the Next.js application
story.so_that: we have a backend-as-a-service for database, authentication, and storage for user data and content management

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the Next.js application is set up, when the Supabase project is initialized, then a new Supabase project is created.
And the Supabase client (`@supabase/supabase-js` and `@supabase/ssr`) is configured in the Next.js application.
And environment variables for Supabase URL and Anon Key are securely managed.
And the `.env.local` file is included in `.gitignore`.

tasks.task: Create a new Supabase project using the Supabase CLI or web interface.
Install Supabase client libraries (`@supabase/supabase-js` and `@supabase/ssr`) in the Next.js application.
Configure the Supabase client in the Next.js application, ensuring secure cookie-based session management.
Set up environment variables for Supabase URL and Anon Key.
Ensure `.env.local` is included in `.gitignore` to prevent committing sensitive information.

constraints.constraint: All file paths must be project-relative.
Use Supabase CLI or web interface for project creation.
Environment variables for Supabase URL and Anon Key must be securely managed and not exposed on the client-side.
The Supabase client must be configured for secure, cookie-based session management in Next.js.
The `.env.local` file must be explicitly included in `.gitignore`.

tests.standards: Automated tests should be placed in the `tests` directory. Integration tests are critical for verifying Supabase client setup.

ideas.idea: Verify the Supabase project is created and accessible (manual check of Supabase dashboard).
Write a basic integration test to verify the Supabase client can be initialized without errors.
Verify environment variables are correctly loaded and accessible within the application (e.g., a simple API route that logs the values, then check logs).
